edges.description: Disrupted SKI-R-SMAD interaction is associated with increased canonical and non-canonical TGF-beta signaling and H3K27ac-marked target-gene expression in steady-state patient fibroblasts and Ski-mutant mice, although acute ligand-stimulation and CRISPR knock-in studies report SKI protein stabilization and attenuated TGF-beta transcriptional responses.
Dysregulated TGF-beta signaling perturbs craniofacial and skeletal development, producing the marfanoid-craniosynostosis skeletal phenotype.

Dysregulated TGF-beta signaling and excessive H3K27ac-driven target-gene expression in the aortic wall drive aortic root dilatation and aneurysm, placing SGS in the spectrum of heritable TGF-beta aortopathies alongside Marfan and Loeys-Dietz syndromes.
Systemic SKI-related connective-tissue involvement in cardiac valves manifests frequently as mitral valve prolapse.
Valvular connective-tissue involvement in SGS frequently leads to mitral regurgitation.
Connective-tissue remodeling of the aortic root and valve leaflets manifests as abnormal aortic valve morphology.
Altered SKI/TGF-beta signaling during cardiac septation is associated with secundum atrial septal defect in some affected individuals.
Systemic connective-tissue and abdominal wall involvement in SGS manifests frequently as inguinal hernia.
Abdominal wall connective-tissue weakness in SGS manifests frequently as umbilical hernia.
Systemic connective-tissue involvement in SGS frequently produces generalized or focal joint hypermobility alongside contractures.
Abnormal skeletal patterning and cranial suture morphogenesis produce craniosynostosis.
Premature cranial suture fusion and altered calvarial growth produce dolichocephaly.
Altered craniofacial and orbital skeletal morphogenesis produces ocular hypertelorism.
Shallow bony orbits secondary to craniosynostosis and midface hypoplasia produce ocular proptosis.
Impaired mandibular skeletal growth produces micrognathia.
Posterior mandibular positioning from craniofacial skeletal dysmorphism produces retrognathia.
Altered palatal and maxillary skeletal morphogenesis produces a high, narrow palate.
Midfacial skeletal underdevelopment manifests as maxillary hypoplasia.
Perturbed long-bone growth produces dolichostenomelia and marfanoid habitus.
Disordered anterior thoracic wall and costal cartilage growth produces pectus excavatum.
Disordered anterior chest wall and sternocostal growth produces pectus carinatum.
Skeletal-development disruption manifests as spinal curvature.
Disrupted skeletal and connective-tissue development produces digital flexion contractures such as camptodactyly.
The marfanoid skeletal habitus includes arachnodactyly.
Disrupted axial skeletal patterning produces C1-C2 cervical spine malformation.
Altered foot skeletal alignment and musculoskeletal development produce pes planus and foot malposition.
Craniosynostosis and craniocervical junction skeletal dysplasia predispose to cerebellar tonsillar herniation (Chiari type I malformation).
Altered cranial vault suture fusion and skull-base venous/CSF dynamics are associated with communicating hydrocephalus in SGS.

nodes.description: Dysregulated SKI function in dermal fibroblasts and vascular smooth muscle cells is associated with enhanced activation of SMAD2/3 and ERK TGF-beta signaling cascades, elevated H3K27 acetylation, and increased expression of TGF-beta-responsive genes in patient fibroblasts and orthologous Ski-mutant mice, paralleling the TGF-beta paradox observed in Marfan and Loeys-Dietz syndromes. nodes.description: Heterozygous missense or in-frame deletion variants clustering in the exon 1 R-SMAD-binding domain (particularly residues Ser31-Pro35) or Dachshund homology domain of SKI abolish SKI binding to phosphorylated SMAD2/3 while retaining SMAD4 interaction via the SAND domain.
